intended_object: For a group G acting on an abelian group A by automorphisms, the subgroup I_G A of A generated by all differences g·a − a (written multiplicatively as (g•a)·a⁻¹). The quotient by it is the algebraic coinvariants A_G. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is `Subgroup.closure` of `differenceSet ρ`, and `differenceSet ρ` is `{ρ g a * a⁻¹ | g ∈ G, a ∈ A}`. This is exactly the subgroup generated by the action differences, which is the relation subgroup for coinvariants. In additive notation it is the span of the elements g·a − a.

The degenerate cases come out right:
- For the trivial action every difference is 1, so the subgroup is ⊥ and the coinvariants are all of A.
- For empty data, `closure ∅ = ⊥`.

The orientation `ρ g a * a⁻¹` versus `a * (ρ g a)⁻¹` does not matter, because the set is closed under inverses up to taking the subgroup.

The section variables also bring `[TopologicalSpace A]` and `[IsTopologicalGroup A]`, which this algebraic construction does not use. Commutativity is not needed for the closure itself either. These extra assumptions are harmless: the whole file is set in commutative topological groups, and this subgroup is just a step towards the closed version and the topological coinvariants.

Mathlib's closest notion is `Representation.Coinvariants.ker`: the submodule spanned by `ρ g v - v` for a k-linear representation. It covers the same object for ℤ-modules in additive form. It is not a general version of this group-level, multiplicative construction, so the definition is not too narrow.
